Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I loop in engineering/security for the export:

Summary of your ask:
- Provide an extract of audit events showing ‘who did what and when’ for the past 12 months (initial sample of last 30 days for legal review).
- Include fields necessary for your compliance team: user_id (internal), actor_type (human/service-account), resource_id, action, timestamp (UTC), request_ip, session_id, redaction_flag, and if possible the model version used.
- Export format preferred: CSV or NDJSON; you indicated CSV is easiest for legal but security prefers NDJSON for structured parsing.
- Delivery: encrypted S3 upload or secure download link.
- Retention: you flagged a 2-year retention requirement; also asked about our deletion/retention controls, and whether exports include masked PII by default.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Confirm required fields and preferred format (CSV vs NDJSON) by EOD Monday, Nov 30.
2) We’ll prepare a 30-day sample export + schema and a short delivery readme (7 business day SLA after confirmation).
3) If sample passes legal/security, we’ll produce a full 12-month export on a mutually agreed schedule and provide documentation on retention/deletion mechanics + KMS usage.

Attached: redwood-audit-schema-v1.csv (schema stub).

If that aligns I’ll open a support ticket and tag Marissa (security lead) and Connor (solutions) to coordinate the export and delivery.

Thanks,

Hi Nikhil — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before you queue engineering:

1) Fields: we need both human and service-account activity; please include an explicit actor_identifier and actor_type field. Also include any impersonation metadata if available.
2) For PII: Legal wants the sample to be minimally processed — do not redact email addresses in the sample export we’ll review that, but if you can include a separate column indicating whether a field contains PII (boolean) that would help.
3) Format: NDJSON preferred if it’s straightforward; if not, CSV with a strict header ordering is ok.
4) Delivery: pre-signed S3 link is fine. Please confirm the encryption (SSE-KMS) key alias used and whether we can request a copy encrypted with our KMS.
5) Timeline: Monday EOD is tight — can we say Nov 30 COB (end of business)? Our compliance meeting is Dec 3.

If you can get a 30-day sample by Nov 30 COB that would be ideal. Thanks for looping in Marissa and Connor.

Hi team / Olivia — plan and artifacts attached below.

What we’re providing (ETA: Nov 30 COB):
- audit_events_finedge_sample.ndjson (30-day sample; includes one line per event).
- delivery_readme.txt — describes each key, the PII_flag boolean, and how redaction_flag is set.
- redwood-audit-schema-v1.csv (schema header + example row).

Notes / security considerations:
- Exports include both human and service-account events; actor_type and actor_identifier are populated. Impersonation metadata is present where the runtime recorded it.
- By default hosted exports are encrypted using SSE-KMS with alias alias/redwood-exports. We cannot re-encrypt with a customer KMS for hosted accounts; if the customer requires their own KMS we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private (we can document options and a migration plan).
- PII handling: sample includes original values for legal review and a PII_flag column. We will not publish unredacted exports to any public location.
- Retention & deletion: our standard retention policy for audit events is 24 months for this workload; we can produce a retention report and run a deletion verification job after the retention period.

Delivery mechanism:
- I’ll upload the sample to a pre-signed, time-limited S3 location and send the link to Olivia privately. Link and checksums will be in the delivery_readme.txt.
